new_candidates.body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacSim/discussions/890
Originally posted by **pheldsynaptics** October 18, 2026 We have an extension that runs a tactile sensor on the Newton backend (MuJoCo solver, hydroelastic contacts). Every physics step, after `collision_pipeline.collide()` and before `solver.step()`, we need to launch a couple of Warp kernels that modify the per-contact data in `contacts` (stiffness and damping) before the solver reads it. Later we also want to compute our own contact forces at that point and write them into `state.body_f`. Isaac Sim has no place to do this. `NewtonStage.physics_callbacks` run after the whole step, which is too late. The only option we found is to replace `collision_pipeline.collide` with a wrapper and set `stage.graph = None` so the CUDA graph is recaptured with our kernels in it. That works on 6.1.0 but depends on private details of `NewtonStage` and will break when they change. Isaac Lab already has this: `NewtonManager.register_state_force_callback()` runs a callback before every solver substep, inside the captured graph. Something equivalent in Isaac Sim's `NewtonStage` would be enough for us, for example: ```python stage.register_pre_solve_callback(fn) # fn(state, contacts), called after collide, before each solver.step stage.unregister_pre_solve_callback(fn) ``` Callbacks would only launch kernels, so they can be recorded into the CUDA graph like the rest of the step. The `ovnewton` engine in 7.0.0a1 (`NewtonStage.subscribe_step_event(pre_step=True, ...)`, also on `develop`) is close, but the pre-step subscribers run before `collide()` and only get `(dt, ctx)`, so the contacts for that step don't exist yet and there is no handle to `state` or `contacts`. A phase after `collide()` that passes `state` and `contacts` would cover this. Checked on Isaac Sim 6.1.0 (`isaacsim.physics.newton` 1.0.6) and in the `develop` and `release/6.2` sources: the step loop is the same, no hook between collide and the solver.
new_candidates.title: [Feature] Newton backend: callback between collide and solver step
